method: Two fresh specialist contexts, one baseline without skill reads and one explicitly reading helen-reprompt. Three cases per context; no repeated independent trials. Cases were used for refinement and are not held out.
limitations: Measures rewritten briefs, not coding outcomes or natural skill activation.
Shared host instructions are present in both conditions.
Provider token usage and billed cost were not available.
No confidence interval or general effectiveness claim is justified.

cases.brief: Evaluate possible improvements to the user's prompting approach without implementing changes. Since no prompts or metrics are available, offer general evaluation criteria and improvement ideas, clearly separating suggestions from findings about their actual prompts.
acceptance: Provide concise criteria covering clarity, context, constraints, output format, and success criteria.
Explain which evidence would support a specific evaluation.
Keep all suggestions advisory.
limitations: Cannot assess actual prompt quality without examples.
Cannot claim effectiveness or measured improvement without results.

cases.brief: Describe an implementation approach for preventing duplicate charges when checkout is retried, preserving the current UI and payment provider. Work through reasonable assumptions autonomously, then identify additional relevant improvements and describe their proposed application. This evaluation permits chat only.
acceptance: Address repeated requests, concurrent retries, ambiguous payment outcomes, and recovery.
Describe a stable checkout idempotency identity, durable attempt tracking, and reconciliation with the existing provider where supported.
Provide verification scenarios demonstrating that retries do not produce additional charges.
Explain further relevant improvements without claiming they were applied.
limitations: No tools, file edits, or implementation execution are permitted.
Provider capabilities and current checkout behavior are unknown.

cases.brief: Describe an evidence-led implementation approach to improve GET /products while preserving its public response schema. Use only the supplied baseline: p95 latency of 1200 ms at 100 requests per second. Identify further relevant improvements after the primary approach and describe how they could be applied, within chat-only constraints.
acceptance: Treat the supplied baseline as the only established measurement.
Outline profiling and candidate improvements with explicit hypotheses rather than assumed bottlenecks.
Describe comparable before-and-after verification and response-schema checks.
Do not invent measurements or numerical performance targets.
limitations: No implementation, inspection, or benchmarking can be performed.
Architecture, workload details, and bottlenecks are unknown.
No performance gain or completed change can be claimed.

cases.brief: Evaluate prompt quality and suggest improvements without implementation. Without the actual prompts or metrics, no quality judgment is supported. Candidate improvements are to state intent, context, exclusions, authorized actions, expected output and observable acceptance explicitly; distinguish facts from assumptions and execution from proposed checks. Assess candidate rewrites for intent preservation, scope preservation, acceptance clarity, action-mode preservation and token use before recommending adoption.
acceptance: Suggestions remain evaluation-only and preserve the original request.
Prompt quality, measured effectiveness and token savings are not claimed without evidence.
Any candidate rewrite can be compared with its original against the five stated dimensions.
limitations: Actual prompts and outcome metrics are unavailable; specific evaluation remains blocked.
Suggestions are provisional, with no implementation or executed validation.

cases.brief: Implement duplicate-charge prevention for checkout retries while preserving the UI and payment provider. Proposed design: use a stable idempotency key for one checkout operation, enforce atomic server-side ownership and persist its result; reuse the provider's idempotency mechanism where supported and reconcile uncertain payment outcomes before another charge. In an authorized execution environment, start with the cheapest available model, delegate relevant specialists, then verify → discover → apply authorized improvements → repeat. Here, provide only this implementation brief and proposed checks.
acceptance: Repeated and concurrent requests produce one payment effect per idempotency key.
Regression checks cover retries after timeouts, concurrent requests, crashes and response loss.
Reusing a key with different payment parameters is rejected; distinct operations remain independent.
UI and provider are preserved; further evidence-backed improvements are verified until discovery finds none actionable within scope.
limitations: No tools, file changes, delegation or tests are executed.
Existing checkout architecture and provider capabilities are unknown; implementation requires access.

cases.brief: Improve GET /products while preserving its public response schema. The supplied baseline is p95 1200 ms at 100 requests/s. Propose profiling database queries, downstream calls, serialization and resource contention; select improvements from observed bottlenecks. Start with the cheapest available model and delegate relevant specialists when execution is permitted; verify → discover → apply authorized improvements → repeat.
acceptance: Compare GET /products against the supplied baseline at 100 requests/s using matched workload, environment and measurement conditions.
Demonstrate reduced p95 latency while preserving public response schema and correctness.
Re-audit and apply further evidence-backed improvements within scope; report concrete blockers.
limitations: Checks are proposed only; no measurements or changes are executed.
Baseline methodology and bottlenecks are unknown; no numeric target or achieved improvement is invented.
